strings.name: Steve Furber
strings.role: Computer engineer · ARM and neuromorphic-computing researcher
strings.summary: Trained in mathematics and aerodynamics at Cambridge, Furber moved into computer engineering at Acorn, co-designing the BBC Micro and ARM with Sophie Wilson. At Manchester from 1990, he studied asynchronous circuits, low-power systems and neural computing and developed SpiNNaker for neural-network simulation. He retired in 2023 as professor emeritus; a 2026 collaborative paper appears in the university’s research record.

strings.influence.rationale: Helped design early ARM processors and researched neuromorphic computing, influencing low-power chips and computer architecture.

strings.highlights.h1.title: Co-designing ARM
strings.highlights.h1.text: Worked with Wilson and Acorn’s team to turn a reduced instruction-set processor into silicon.
strings.highlights.h2.title: The SpiNNaker platform
strings.highlights.h2.text: Advanced a research system using many low-power processors to simulate spiking neural networks.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Collaborative neural-computing paper
strings.timeline.t1.text: Contributed to full-density spiking-network modeling, linking brain models with computing architectures.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Retired as professor emeritus
strings.timeline.t2.text: Left regular university employment while continuing academic work as emeritus professor of computer engineering.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Million-core SpiNNaker launched
strings.timeline.t3.text: Manchester’s team switched on a million-core system for large neural-network simulations.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Computer History Museum honor
strings.timeline.t4.text: Recognized with Wilson for work on the BBC Micro and ARM.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Joined Manchester
strings.timeline.t5.text: Took the ICL chair in computer engineering and studied asynchronous and low-power systems.
strings.timeline.t6.title: ARM realized
strings.timeline.t6.text: Worked with Acorn’s team on early ARM designs, establishing a processor technology foundation.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Joined Acorn
strings.timeline.t7.text: After his aerodynamics doctorate, entered hardware development and helped build products including the BBC Micro.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Earned mathematics BA
strings.timeline.t8.text: Completed mathematics at Cambridge before further research in aerodynamics.
